hook_text: Two lessons, a bag of dowel and a toy motor. Here is how a working mine headgear gets built without anyone getting hurt.
clip_script: Safety first: dowel in a bench hook, gear plate clamped for drilling, knife along the rule, hot glue at its station, eyes covered, and one named hand on the switch for every motor test. Then three words: square, plumb, braced. Base square with a try square. Faces flat over a full-size layout, a diagonal in every rectangle, set over the break. Stand them, two people holding, one gluing; check plumb from two sides before the last diagonals lock it. Tower to base. Back-leg cut to the real measured distance, not the list. Sheave free on its axle. Winder last: gear plate square to the rope, train free by hand, collars on every shaft, string wound the right way. Then tests with numbers: free by hand, direction, lift times at 100, 200, 300 grams, brake, sway in millimetres, topple. Stalled? Batteries, friction, smaller drum, load path, ratio, in that order, before and after written down.
visual_style: Whiteboard bench: a saw in a bench hook, a clamped plate under a drill; two faces lie flat then rise and join; a square checks plumb; a back-leg is measured in place; gears spin, a stopwatch runs and a table fills with grams and seconds.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write your test table headings before you build.
